binders: A natural number m with 0 < m; every state and flux is a real vector indexed by Fin m.
A conservation law law carrying a physical flux, a Fréchet derivative, a matrix Jacobian representing that derivative, and a complete real eigenbasis for every Jacobian.
A bi-infinite one-dimensional grid with positive-width cells and matching adjacent boundaries.
An initial state initialState : Real → (Fin m → Real), interval-integrable on every grid cell.
An arbitrary Information type and a method with a certified solver for every Riemann problem, an information extractor, a numerical-flux readout, and equal-state consistency.
hypotheses: The component count is positive: 0 < m.
For every integer cell i, initialState is interval-integrable from grid.cellLeft(i) to grid.cellRight(i).
Structurally, each grid cell has positive width and grid.cellRight(i−1) = grid.cellLeft(i).
Structurally, physicalFlux is Fréchet differentiable, its derivative is represented by the supplied Jacobian matrix, and each Jacobian has a complete real eigenbasis.
Structurally, method.solve returns a certified solution for every left/right problem; extraction and flux readout are total; and the method reproduces physicalFlux on equal-state problems.
The time step is positive: 0 < timeStep.
conclusions: The proposition repeats 0 < m and 0 < timeStep.
There exists a cell-average field U : Int → (Fin m → Real) such that U_i = (Δx_i)⁻¹ ∫_{cellLeft(i)}^{cellRight(i)} initialState(x) dx for every i.
The proposition repeats grid.cellRight(i−1) = grid.cellLeft(i) for every i.
For every interface i there exists a certified solution q_i of the problem with left state U_{i−1} and right state U_i.
For x<0, q_i(x,0)=U_{i−1}; for x>0, q_i(x,0)=U_i.
For all real a,b,t, q_i(·,t) is interval-integrable and d/dt ∫_a^b q_i(x,t)dx = physicalFlux(q_i(a,t)) − physicalFlux(q_i(b,t)).
There exists information(i) equal to method.extractInformation(solved(i)), and numericalFlux(i) equal to method.numericalFluxFromInformation(information(i)).
For every constant state V, the flux obtained by solving (V,V), extracting information, and reading it out equals law.physicalFlux(V).
There exists U_new with U_new(i) = U_i − (timeStep/Δx_i)(F_{i+1}−F_i) for every integer cell i.
mathematical_definitions: A state is U : Fin m → Real, and f(U)=law.physicalFlux(U).
The law supplies Df(U), a matrix J(U), and Df(U)[V]=J(U)V for every state U and direction V.
For each U there are real eigenvalues λ_p and a basis v_p satisfying J(U)v_p=λ_pv_p.
Cell i has endpoints xL_i=grid.cellLeft(i), xR_i=grid.cellRight(i), and volume Δx_i=xR_i−xL_i>0.
Grid adjacency is xR_{i−1}=xL_i, equivalently xR_i=xL_{i+1}.
Interface i lies between cells i−1 and i and carries the Riemann problem (U_{i−1},U_i).
A certified q_i has the prescribed two-sided t=0 trace and satisfies the physical-flux interval balance for every interval and real time.
The t=0 trace imposes no value at x=0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a positive finite number of real state components, take a differentiable conservation law whose flux derivative is represented by a real Jacobian matrix with a complete real eigenbasis at every state. On a bi-infinite one-dimensional grid of positive-width contiguous cells, assume the initial vector-valued state is integrable on every cell. Given a positive time step and a method that supplies a certified integral-conservation solution of every left/right Riemann problem, extracts information from that solution, reads a numerical flux from the information, and reproduces the physical flux for equal states, one can construct the exact normalized initial average in every cell. At each interface one can solve the Riemann problem formed by the two neighboring averages, extract its information, and form its numerical flux. One can then construct updated cell averages by U_new(i)=U_i−(timeStep/Δx_i)(F_{i+1}−F_i). Each interface solution genuinely carries the two-sided Riemann initial trace and an interval-integral physical-flux balance.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition genuinely constructs normalized cell averages from interval integrals.
The grid has positive-width contiguous cells, but it need not cover all of Real: the bi-infinite boundary sequence may accumulate at finite endpoints.
The physical flux is genuinely Fréchet differentiable and its derivative genuinely agrees with the supplied Jacobian action.
The Jacobian condition gives real diagonalizability but does not require distinct, ordered, or uniformly separated eigenvalues; it is weaker than strict hyperbolicity.
Existence of a certified solution for every Riemann problem is built into method. The proposition does not derive Riemann-solution existence from the law assumptions.
The solution satisfies an interval-integral balance for every interval and real time, but the pointwise PDE is not separately asserted.
No entropy condition, admissibility, uniqueness, self-similarity, boundedness, regularity, or finite-propagation property is required of solutions.
The initial trace is unconstrained at x=0.
Although solved(i) can be chosen as method.solve(problem_i), the conclusion does not explicitly assert that equality; it only existentially selects a certified solution of the correct dependent type.
Information is abstract. The numerical flux is tied to extracted information but is not required to equal a Godunov flux, a solution trace, or the physical flux for unequal states.
The method's only explicit flux correctness condition is equal-state consistency.
No locality, continuity, monotonicity, entropy stability, positivity, or invariant-domain property of the numerical flux is assumed.
The update has the standard nonuniform local flux-difference form, but no global finite-sum conservation theorem is stated.
timeStep is only positive; there is no CFL condition or upper bound involving cell widths or wave speeds.
Only one update is constructed. No time iteration, convergence, truncation error, or stability result is formalized.
initialState is assumed integrable cell by cell, not globally over Real.
The proposition repeats several facts already carried by its binders: positive m, positive timeStep, grid adjacency, solution validity, and equal-state consistency.
Most existential witnesses are canonical constructions from the supplied grid and method and add no analytical guarantees beyond their structural assumptions.
If m=0, cellwise integrability fails, or no method with certified solvers exists, the corresponding premise or binder cannot be supplied and the statement has no substantive instance.
The physical names do not select any particular conservation system; any structures satisfying the displayed laws qualify.
ambiguities: The physical meaning of the m state components and physicalFlux is unspecified.
The eigenbasis condition may be intended as hyperbolicity, but it does not formalize distinct characteristic speeds.
Information may encode waves, traces, or arbitrary solver data; its semantics are unconstrained.
The numerical flux is not identified with evaluation of solved(i).solution at any particular space-time point.
timeStep/grid.cellVolume(i) has the form of a time-step-to-cell-width ratio, but no units are represented.
The solution predicate quantifies over all real times, including negative times, even if only forward evolution is intended.
The formula fixes interface i between cells i−1 and i, but no separate geometric interface object is defined.
